prompted_for: Equipment line drawing for the Pharmaceutical industry page (ind-pharma); came out as a sterile vial filling machine, superseded by a mixing vessel fed by a PW point-of-use valve (gemini/67)
composition: box-frame machine enclosure in isometric, doors swung open on both sides
two hood units on the roof
conveyor of vials crossing diagonally through the middle
filling needles, vibratory bowl feeder and stopper chute inside
inlet valve and pipe on the lower left
ui_patterns: section illustration masked in a token colour
t2i_keywords: machine enclosure with open glass doors
rows of small repeated parts on a conveyor
t2i_prompt: Isometric technical line drawing of <CONTENT>, black ink on pure white: a framed machine enclosure seen three-quarter from above with its glass doors swung open to reveal the mechanism inside, a row of small repeated parts travelling diagonally on a conveyor, roof units on top and an inlet pipe with a hand-wheel valve at the base. Uniform thin strokes, no shading, no fill, no colour, no text, clean white margin, crisp closed contours for a single-colour mask.
signature_idea: The customer's production line opened up so you see where purified water finally ends up.
strengths: line style matches the drawing set and masks well
weaknesses: sterile vial filling implies WFI/sterile scope Aquemi does not sell (hence replaced)
very busy interior gets muddy when scaled down
the water connection is a tiny afterthought
brand_fit_why: On-style line art, but the subject misrepresents the PW offer and the clutter fights the calm brand.
